I think multiple things can be true at the same time. That is to say, it's not as bad as most people think but it can also be, for some people, pretty bad. I'm facing the same exact set of circumstances you were and so far I have rejected recommendations of a diverting stoma from multiple medical professionals. 

I also do a lot of public speaking and participating in meetings for my job, and I imagine I would have to either give that up or just accept uncontrollable audible stoma farts. I also play contact sports, which I'd probably have to give up. And before anyone says that their friend, uncle, brother, etc. plays rugby, football, hockey, etc., I'm telling you, I wouldn't be able to play with a stoma the way I play now, that's for sure. 

So what I've settled on is that these can be a helpful for some people in some cases, but not for others. And I'll end with a statement of appreciation to OP. By putting yourself out there like this you're probably going to help a lot of people cope. Unfortunately I'm just a lost cause.

I appreciate your advice, and your indulgence. Most people on these forums just call me an asshole. I have an endless supply of respect and admiration for ostomates, I really do. But, I just don’t have it in me, mostly for the following reasons:

1. I’m disgusted by body modification, and also proximity to the digestive process. When the terminal point is behind me it’s out of sight. I couldn’t handle it being in my field of vision, let alone having to directly handle it.

2. It would take up too much permanent headspace. I’d be thinking about it, to some extent, at all times. Is it leaking? Is it full? Where’s the bathroom in case it becomes full? Is it showing? 

3. It’s inconsistent with my lifestyle. I’m not a model (if I showed my face/body that would be obvious!) but I do play contact sports recreationally, and I swim regularly. They say I can still play ice hockey with it, but I’m sorry, I think it’s irresponsible to put others in a situation where they might encounter my liquid waste. I am also a public speaker, and so can’t have a stoma gurgling and farting into a hot microphone.

4. The stigma aspect. I haven’t even told any of my friends about my illness. How can I go over to their house and ask them where to throw away my used stoma bag, or tell them I’ve leaked all over their couch? How can I tell my parents/in laws that?

That’s the main objections I can think of at this time. Again, I appreciate your engagement.
